title: LLM-as-a-Prophet: Understanding Predictive Intelligence with Prophet Arena
claim: A forecasting benchmark is decomposed into staged modules, from live event extraction through context construction to prediction and evaluation against realized outcomes.
layout: 3 colored panels, left-to-right, cross-panel arrows linking a running example
description: Three rounded, color-coded panels run left to right and are numbered and titled at the top. Panel 1 (green) is Event/Market Extraction. It has a prediction-market crystal-ball icon above a card for a sample event, the 2025 US Open men's tennis champion. The card lists two markets, Sinner and Alcaraz, with Yes/No price tags and the final outcome. Panel 2 (orange) is Prediction Context Construction. It shows a web search icon leading to news sources, then human insights shown as a user group and a speech bubble. All of this feeds a gray text box holding the prediction prompt. Panel 3 has a pink box for the LLM prediction model, showing a robot and a list of reasoning, tool use and internal knowledge. A blue box below it shows probabilities (48% Sinner, 52% Alcaraz). A purple evaluation box at the bottom has a bar chart and the metrics accuracy, calibration and market return. Arrows link the panels, and a long bottom arrow carries the outcome to evaluation. The font is hand-drawn.
caption: Overview of the \prophet\ pipeline. The outcomes of events are unknown at extraction time. LLM predictions are generated at pre-scheduled forecast times, and evaluation occurs only after the events resolve, comparing model forecasts against the realized outcomes.
abstract: Forecasting is not only a fundamental intellectual pursuit but also is of significant importance to societal systems such as finance and economics. With the rapid advances of large language models (LLMs) trained on Internet-scale data, it raises the promise of employing LLMs to forecast real-world future events, an emerging paradigm we call "LLM-as-a-Prophet". This paper systematically investigates such predictive intelligence of LLMs. To this end, we build Prophet Arena, a general evaluation benchmark that continuously collects live forecasting tasks and decomposes each task into distinct pipeline stages, in order to support our controlled and large-scale experimentation. Our comprehensive evaluation reveals that many LLMs already exhibit impressive forecasting capabilities, reflected in, e.g., their small calibration errors, consistent prediction confidence and promising market returns. However, we also uncover key bottlenecks towards achieving superior predictive intelligence via LLM-as-a-Prophet, such as LLMs' inaccurate event recalls, misunderstanding of data sources and slower information aggregation compared to markets when resolution nears.
